_comment: Phase 4.1 corpus-sweep target list (extended 2026-07-27 with 50 more sites — grep 'PHASE 4.3', weighted news/media + entity/structured per request; news URLs discovered live via tools/discover-article-urls.spec.ts against Profile 3, entity URLs are stable direct deep-links). Extended 2026-07-28 with 100 more seeds (grep 'PHASE 4.4' in tools/discover-article-urls.spec.ts) covering non-English scripts (CJK/RTL/Cyrillic), sports/finance/science verticals, Q&A + forum threads, doc-sites and structured entity pages; discovered live the same way. Each entry is a real ARTICLE / content URL the sweep captures, renders, scores (text-coverage, blank-ratio, aspect-distortion, chrome-hits), and screenshots (source/clip/cast). Deep article URLs (not homepages/section hubs) are used deliberately: (1) a single article is the realistic capture target — a homepage's lead-story teaser is a hero + no body, which the scorer mistakes for a broken clip; (2) CF/bot walls hit homepages/section indexes far harder than individual articles, so a deep-link also clears several sites a hub URL gets blocked on. These URLs were discovered live from each site's section page via tests/e2e/tools/discover-article-urls.mjs (run against the warm Cloudflare-cleared Chrome Profile 3) on 2026-07-21 — NOT hand-written, so they were real+loading when added. Article URLs rot: when a formerly-good site starts skipping with 'load failed', re-run the discovery tool to refresh its URL. Sweep runs against the same warm profile. A URL that won't load is a SKIP, not a scored finding; paywalls + IP-level 403s will still skip and that's expected. 'format' defaults to 'article'. Extended 2026-07-30 with PHASE 4.5 — 6 book/film/music review+catalogue entity pages (StoryGraph, LibraryThing, RateYourMusic, Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music) completing the rate-and-review site class alongside the existing goodreads-book/goodreads-author/letterboxd/rottentomatoes/metacritic/discogs/lastfm entries. FIELD 'headed': true marks a domain that must run in the sweep's headed-first pass and NEVER take a headless hit. This is routing data, not a hint — a headless hit on such a site returns a hard interstitial ('ray id', 'you've been blocked'), which the detector classifies HARD, which sets challenged=false, which EXCLUDES it from the Pass-2 headed retry: the domain is then unreachable for the whole run no matter how it is paced. Worse for stateful sites (Medium blocks on a second load in quick succession and stays blocked for that profile until cleared by hand), where the wasted headless load locks out the headed pass that would have worked. Seeded from two evidence sources: domains the sweep actually captured via the manual headed pass (score.json note) and notes stating headless does not work. Prefer adding 'headed': true here over editing the sets in corpus-sweep.spec.ts, which read this field.

domains.name: msn-slideshow
domains.note: PHASE 4.6 — FEED READER: MSN /ss- SLIDESHOW (a gallery, not prose). Guards the PRELOADED-NEXT-ARTICLE regression (user report 2026-08-03, 'the wrong thing is clipped'): MSN's infinite-scroll feed preloads the next stories into the SAME DOM (div.consumptionFeed_nextArticle), and the viewed gallery has NO <article> of its own — so Tier 1's first selector matched a PRELOADED story's <article class='article-reader-container'> and shipped a clip whose TITLE was this slideshow but whose BODY was an unrelated article. Fixed generically via PRELOADED_NEXT_SELECTOR at three layers (findArticleElement / scoreContentBlock / markExcluded), using closestDeep — native closest() stops at the first of MSN's ~350 open shadow roots. WATCH OUT: a regression here scores HEALTHY (the wrong body is full-length, well-formed prose), so the score alone will not catch it — check the clip screenshot actually shows Star Trek / Kirk, not whatever MSN preloaded next. Slideshow text lives in per-slide fragments, so expect lower text-coverage than a prose article.

domains.name: offguardian
domains.note: PHASE 4.6 — HOTLINK-PROTECTED IMAGES: WordPress long-form article (banner hero + donation-button images). Guards the CAST-IMAGE regression (user report 2026-08-03, 'the clip shows an image but the cast doesn't'): the site 403s any request carrying a foreign Referer (200 with no referer, 403 for https://discerned.online/), so every cast image silently failed to load while the CLIP looked perfect — the clip renders inlined base64, the cast must publish a real URL because data: URIs are too large for relays. Fixed in the WEB APP, not the extension (which was emitting correct markdown + imeta all along): DetailPanel now sets referrerPolicy='no-referrer' on every cast-image path (markdown via MD_COMPONENTS, hero, gallery, inline). WATCH OUT: the sweep's CLIP screenshot cannot catch this — check {domain}--3-cast.png specifically, and confirm the FAKING WATER BANKRUPTCY banner is visible rather than a blank gap.

domains.name: postguam
domains.note: PHASE 4.6 — BLUR-UP LAZY IMAGES: TownNews/BLOX local-news article. Guards the DUPLICATE-IMAGE regression (user report 2026-08-03, 'shows each of the first two images twice on clips and cast'): each photo is rendered as a PAIR — the real (still lazy, src is a 4x3 base64 spacer, real URL only in srcset) plus an aria-hidden='true' low-res `tnt-blurred-image` placeholder holding the http URL. Live CSS layers them; sanitisation strips it and BOTH render. Neither existing dedup pass could catch it (they key on a shared URL stem or a shared >10-char alt, and this pair shares NEITHER), so markExcluded now drops img[aria-hidden='true'] — the page's own declaration that the image is decorative. Generic: tnt-blurred-image ships on hundreds of TownNews local-news sites. WATCH OUT: duplicated images do NOT lower the score — check the clip screenshot for each photo appearing twice.
